Do you like a "mining" industry type of game that's simple to play, intuitive and rather relaxing?   This is it!!   Go get that gold and level up those gem stones.

There are two games in one here!

Legacy Mode: Very much the traditional digging game  with the vibe of A Game about Digging a Hole with a one dimensional upgrades that sometimes don't feel that useful but in the long run do add up. The "get back up" mechanic is super bleh so I just accepted the death and would keep going with the next body to get deeper. 

Version 2.0: A delightful redesign and a signifigantly deeper game! You dig deep but as you come across new ores, you can use them to craft recipes you find in blueprints to upgrade your character! Every ore comes with a new set of blueprints in its own layer that you have to get to to upgrade your battery, rope, etc. You have to decide do I USE this ore or do I sell it to afford a better crafting recipe later? Which type of digging tool will you use because now there's multiple kinds? Do you WANT the better boots that lower fall damage when your current ones already have enough jump height to the point you're hitting your head?  A refreshing take in the digging space. 

Looks decent, odd clipping on character models, less options in Version 2 and overall not a lot of settings to work with in general. 

The only game breaking bug I found was when I dug straight down too fast, game couldn't load, and it dumped me out into out of bounds. I

Good game!

1.0は友達と大人数で盛り上がりながら下まで掘るというバカゲーとしての魅力を最大限持った楽しいパーティーゲーだった。
しかし、2.0になってからゲームのテンポが著しく低下し1.0のバカゲー感を求めていたために愕然とした。マルチプレイを想定していないと思うほどかまどの容量が小さい。これがゲームテンポを終わりに導いているすべてと言っていいかもしれない。
かまどが小さいせいでキレすぎて一時間で辞めたからあとは知らないけど、制作陣が作業ゲーとして他のゲームからいろいろと学習してきたのかもしれないが自分たちの客が何を望んでいるのか正確にとらえられていないと感じた。

最佳化?優化就是一坨被風扇吹爛的稀糞。5070ti+9700x開遊戲瞬間風扇像他媽要起飛挖礦，不知道的以為我在後台跑比特幣。這配置都壓不住，你們程式設計師是拿腳寫的程式碼？

玩法？換皮都換不懂。吸塵器系統純屬脫褲子放屁，自己掄鎬子鏟子還他媽扣電，電池本來就跟尿崩一樣，兩下見底。你們是不是覺得玩家時間不值錢，電量焦慮很好玩？

教學寫了跟沒寫一樣，新人進來直接懵逼，連吐槽都找不到字。跟朋友開黑？三個人玩得沉默得像在參加葬禮，最後統一差評。

這玩意兒也配叫2.0？怕不是愚人節提早半年準備的冷笑話。優點？我拿放大鏡找了三天，連個像素點都算不上的優點都沒有。從UI到手感，從機製到反饋，每一處都在告訴玩家：“我們根本不在乎你玩得爽不爽，我們只在乎這坨屎有沒有熱過。”

總結：別買，別下，別浪費時間。如果你已經買了，當自己踩了狗屎，趕緊卸載，別回頭。這遊戲不是給人類玩的。

Вроде купил всё в магазине, но это самые отстойные инструменты, будь добр найти рандомные крутые чертежи, чтобы потом собрать камни, которые ты уже прошел, ты возвращаешься, собираешь камни, переплавляешь и делаешь инструмент получше, а это оказывается чертеж бессмысленного сканера, который тебе в начале не нужен, но он же золотой! 

Ты прокапал до 500 метров с товарищем, который играет с тобой и думаешь... ну ладно, тут хоть чек-поинты частые, ага ,фиг тебе, ты прокапал до 500 метров, а потом копаешь, копаешь, копаешь, твой товарищ убил тебя раз 10, потому что вы копали рядом с друг другом, ты начинаешь с чек-поинта и летишь вниз, но тут теперь добавили урон от падения, когда ты падаешь с высоты, то твоя батарея уменьшается и пока ты дойдешь до места где остановился, у тебя уже минус 20-30% батарей. 
Ты находишься очередной сундук, надеешься, что вот сейчас будет золотой чертеж продвинутой батареи, но нет! Это золотой вакуум! Худшее, что может выпасть на таком этапе игры, честно говоря моя девушка лучше вакуумит, чем вакуум в игре!

Honestly, I don't know how the overall reviews are mostly positive. 

Even from the menu screen, the game has countless bugs that would have been incredibly easy to detect if they did any sort of testing. To name just a few of the most obvious:
- Some buttons have text completely hanging over the edge of the button. 
- Sound randomly cuts out when drilling. 
- When I started the game my shovel was showing as being through my wrist rather than held, and I couldn't actually use it until I swapped it to a different slot and swapped back.
- My friend stood on what looked like a sort of elevator and got thrown under the map.
- I clicked the invite friend button, it sent me to a menu/loading screen, then back into the game with no prompt to actually invite a friend. It turns out it just creates a code to send to friends, not an actual invite button.
- Sometimes when digging on the surface in 2.0.0, we had to go underground then back out to replenish energy, even though we were on the surface the whole time. Feels like a very weird thing to happen if intentional. 

As for gameplay itself, several elements are just unenjoyable. 

1.0.0:
- My friend played solo for a bit, and when he joined my game he was flying on my screen because his progress carried over, so he was stood atop something I didn't have on my end.
- Following on from that, we have no idea how to start over. We couldn't figure it out so assume it's impossible without deleting save files on your PC. So what, you just keep digging on the same map forever?

2.0.0:
- Animations for crafting can't be skipped. You have to watch them every single time. 
- Blueprints are a one time use. They have rarity but we couldn't figure out what that actually changes?
- Minor complaint, but copper should not be more expensive/better than iron. That's backwards.
- "quests" popped up at the top of the screen as a sort of guide. It started normal, then jumped from crafting an item to reaching 300m. We didn't even reach 100m before giving up. Having been able to buy the copper tools at that point and having nothing new, it just felt tedious and boring. 

- Over both modes, having to go above ground for energy constantly gets tedious real fast. We never found out if there were methods further down to replenish while mining, because we couldn't stand playing the game that long.

Do not buy this game. 1 hour of gameplay should not have so many bugs at the very least. It just comes across as an untested mess.

I'll put in a Recommend for this, but I'm on the fence and think the game deserves the Mixed rating it currently has in Recent Reviews.

The game in legacy V1 mode: A simple digging incremental game where you dig up ores and gems and sell them to buy upgrades to dig up more ores and gems and sell them and buy upgrades to... Yeah, it is what it is. You can turn your brain off and forget about the world around you for a while. There are some occasional neat but simple side areas you can explore for some loot and visuals. And you can build a dinosaur with the bones that spawn in the large caverns you find.

The game in new V2 mode: Ores can now be smelted with coal, producing ingots that can either be sold or used to craft items from blueprints that can be found in random chests. Gems can now be used to craft orbs that give your character stat buffs. V2 is a strict upgrade in depth for most of the incremental upgrade mechanics. There are some places where V2 misses:

First and most importantly, V2 has horrible performance issues that V1 does not have. The further I dug down, the worse the performance became. This applies to both average framerate and the huge stutter that started happening every 5 seconds or so like the game ran out of memory and was using a page file (it wasn't). I've included my specs, but I see people complaining about the performance that have significantly stronger PCs. This is the reason I'm on the fence about recommending the game, otherwise it would be a solid recommend for a inexpensive multiplayer-enabled digging incremental game.

The static side areas from V1 have been replaced with randomly generated alcoves along the side of the digging area. The alcoves are always small one-room areas that contain one or three chests. Their appearance varies greatly as you dig further down, but they are still one-room areas that lack the character of the side areas from V1. I would love to see some larger and more interesting side areas randomly show up from time to time. And some randomly generated caverns similar to V1 would be a nice touch for variety.

In V2, there are multiple tool types that try to specialize in different aspects of digging, like horizontally or vertically. This mechanic fell flat for me. The entire point of the game is to dig vertically. The only reason you would want a tool specializing in horizontal digging is if you needed to strip mine to farm ores and gems for money and upgrades, but that simply never became necessary for me. Maybe if you're trying to min-max certain stats by rolling legendary orbs to test the boundaries of the game, you might want to strip mine, but I feel that the game would overstay its welcome at that point.

There's also a Statue of Liberty that serves as a sort-of prestige mechanic, where you can reset your dig site in exchange for chests and gems. But again, I didn't feel particularly lacking in blueprints or gems when digging down, so resetting the dig site never felt appealing.

2.0 Update Review
Pros:

The progression is way better than before.
The crafting system and blueprints are a nice addition that make you spend more time farming and upgrading your gear between teleports.
I like the idea of passive stat effects from crafting orbs.
The shared chest is a good feature for sharing gear and materials.

Cons:

Optimization is bad. There are frame drops and desyncs here and there, especially when someone teleports or when crafting.
V-Sync keeps turning on by itself.
While the idea of Orbs is nice, the implementation is horrible. Most effects are barely noticeable, and they cost a lot of materials and money. The whole system feels rushed and incomplete.
A few effects were good, like better prices, more backpack space, or increased battery capacity, but I only crafted one of them at the start of the game and couldn’t get similar effects in the deeper levels. Rerolls and synthesizes are also terrible.
Additionally, why are Orbs sold for only $1?
A personal (non-shared) chest to store orbs and gear that aren’t meant to be shared would be a great addition.
Gear needs better descriptions. For example, how am I supposed to know the difference between a pickaxe (better for digging vertically) and a shovel (better for digging deeper)?
Teleportation stones (or whatever they were called) are missing in the new update.

Overall:
The new content is good, but the game still needs more optimization and a lot of quality-of-life improvements. The Orb system could also use a lot of changes.
I would still recommend it, as it can be really fun to play with friends despite the issues.

1.0 my buddy and I beat the game in 1.5 hours and had a blast. This 2.0 update we played for 7 hours straight and made it to 3500/5000m. This is such a fun and relaxing game. Probably the  best $7 I have spent in my life.

The game runs fine at the start, but the longer I played, the more my frames dropped, till it was barely 30fps . This was at lowest graphics too, so I dont think its an issue with my rig. Hope the devs do more for optimization soon.

Other than that, gameplay loop for V1.0 was fun but V2.0 gets stale real fast due to the lack of teleportation totems.  This, combined with the fact that the manholes usually appear every 500m means you having to backtrack more than 2 mins each time you head down for more ores. After a while of that, it basically just kills all motivation you have to play the game.

V2.0 introduces blueprints, which in theory adds more complexity to the gameplay, but coupled with the fact that there's RNG involved, the items you get and the tier of their rarity, and you can no longer purchase tools past Copper in the store, could mean that you get stuck with low tier/ rarity tools for way longer than necessary. For example, I was stuck with a Copper battery all the way till Uranium tier. If playing with friends, you could pool and swap blueprints with the chest system, making this process much easier.

TLDR: if you're playing with friends, its more tolerable but if you're solo I probably wouldn't recommend playing V2.0.

I really liked A Game About Digging a Hole so I thought this game might be similar. It is...but not in a good way. First of all, as a female player I have to admit I was a bit annoyed by the lack of a female character option. I mean, hey, devs, girls like games about digging, too. Like, every character is male. But okay, I looked past that and tried to enjoy the digging. Unlike AGADAH, this game has a lot of procedurally-generated elements. So you dig down, collect ore A, sell ore A, get better tools made out of ore A, dig down, collect ore B, sell ore B, get better tools made out of ore B....there's no lore, nothing to do but dig and collect and forge and repeat. The huge scale of the digging means there's none of the fun of trying to "clear" an area, like I did with AGADAH. Why bother? There's nothing new to find, no secrets to uncover. In the end, you just press a button. I won't say more about the ending cutscene, but, yeah, it's pretty basic. I mean, I definitely liked the relaxation of this game--I played it while watching YouTube, and I don't mind grindy games. But once I figured out I didn't need to bother coming back up at all--I could just dig down until I died, use the rope to get back down to where I left off, and repeat--I made it to the 5,000 meter mark in pretty short order. Once you get to the bottom, there's really nothing much to see. I thought AGADAH was better--it was more compact, with a more interesting level progression and more stuff to find. The ending was also better. So,  I can't really recommend this game, unless you're looking for a quick "digging game" fix and you don't mind an endless grind for little payoff. Note: I played this solo, as I don't do co-op, so that might also make the game more enjoyable for you. But since I'm not a 12-year-old boy, I didn't bother with any of the silly emotes or whatever.

問題は2.0について。
根本は変わらないのですがクラフトゲームとして一新したので1000ｍまで掘ったのですが、悪い点が悪目立ちしてます。
まず良い点として
・クラフトしてプレイヤーを強くする楽しさが増えたので単純に掘るモチベーションに繋がる。
・ドリルなどの新アイテムが増えた
・オーブのよるエンドコンテンツが増えた
これは良かったのですが問題は悪目立ちする悪い点です。
・バッテリー（体力）回復や全体的燃費が悪くなったことで帰り道を作って帰るよりリスポーンしてまた戻って鉱石回収したほうがストレスも少なく効率も良く根本的解決してない。
・ドリル、ロープの燃費が悪すぎて結局ツルハシとダイナマイトでいい。
・スキャン強化しないと宝箱が見つけ辛くドリルとロープの件もあり設計図の当たりと外れが大きい
・全体的UIがひどい、カバンを一括でボックスに送れないので一々クリックで送らないといけない、鉱石を一括かまどに送れないのもストレス。
・クラフト要素が増えて鉱石価格は1.0とほぼ同じなので金策が必要になったこと。
と荒削りなゲームになってしまったことです
まだ2.0は始まったばかりなので、パッチなので改善するまで買うのはオススメ出来ないです。
1.0のレガシーは全然面白いので勿体ないなと感じます

I don’t know what the hell Keep Digging was supposed to be, but finishing it in about an hour felt less like an achievement and more like surviving a migraine simulator. The whole experience is just mind-numbing repetition wrapped in boring mechanics that feel like they were slapped together in five minutes.

The gameplay? Absolute garbage. You just keep doing the same crap over and over with zero payoff. No depth, no challenge, nothing remotely satisfying—just dig, dig, dig until you’re questioning your life choices. I’ve had more fun staring at a blank wall.

And the worst part? This game actually gave me a headache. Not metaphorically—an actual, pounding, “why did I waste my time on this?” headache. Whether it’s the visuals, the lack of variety, or just how painfully dull everything is, it’s honestly impressive how quickly it goes from boring to physically irritating.

If you’re thinking about playing this, do yourself a favor and don’t. There are a million better ways to spend an hour than this frustrating, half-baked mess.

[h3]マルチ可能な掘りゲー[/h3]
全実績解除までプレイしましたのでレビューします。
なお、自分はソロプレイによる感想です。
割とシンプル目の掘りゲーですが、ちょっと癖がある部分があります。
しかし、掘りゲー好きの人にはお勧めできるゲームだと思います。セール中でワンコイン未満、セール中でなくてもほぼワンコイン価格なので、十分にその価値はあると思います。


[u][b]良い点[/b][/u]
・掘りゲーです。掘りゲー好きな人にはこれはまずの良い点です。
・基本的な掘りゲーにありそうな成長要素は備わっています。成長具合もリーズナブルだと言えると思います。
・日本語ローカライズは悪くはないです。
・掘りゲーとしてはスタンダードな垂直方向の掘りが基本ですが、たまに横穴などの遺跡ギミックがあります。良いアクセントになっていると思います。
・ひたすら掘りたい人には十分に応えてくれる程度には掘れると思います。周回までやってみましたが、12時間ほど遊べました。


[u][b]悪い点[/b][/u]
・だいたいは、常に画面にUIガイダンスが表示されていますが、一部表示されないUIインタラクションがあります。そこだけ分かりにくいです。
・垂直移動のコストが、特に序盤において、他ゲーに比べてかなり重いように感じられます。電池の消耗量が多すぎるように感じます。
・上記と絡みますが、通常でいうダッシュ移動が非常にコスト高です。このシフト移動部分はかなり簡悔味を強く感じる人が多いと思います。
・全ての行動がなぜか電気・電池依存になっており、鉱夫なのに電池切れでロストする謎仕様です。あと、電池容量の育成段階での充電コスト増しが地味に重いです。バランス的に電池を成長させるメリットが最終段階になるまであまりないように感じていました。この充電の仕様は、プレイを気楽に継続する上ではちょっとした障壁にもなるかもなと感じながらやってました。このせいで若干気の向かない気の重くなるプレイになっていたように感じていました。
・ダイナマイト使用時には鉱物が生成されないのと、MAXにしても大した範囲を爆破できるわけではないので、利用価値が低く使いどころがほぼありません。
・ペイントも使いどころがほぼないです。スパゲッティな掘りをすることを想定していたのかもしれませんが、普通はそうはならんやろと思ってました。
・資金補助NPCが要るんですが、効果を感じれるくらいにゲームを進める頃には金は要らないくらいになっていて、バランスが悪いかなと感じました。
・ストーリがかなり意味不(ry　おっと、誰か来たようだ・・・

Hallo erstmal!

Diese Rezension wird sich in 9 Kategorien gliedern.
Ich hoffe, dass sie euch bei der Kaufentscheidung hilft.

Grafik:
Die Grafik ist ganz hübsch und die Ruinen sehen auch gar nicht mal so schlecht aus.

Performance:
Ich hatte nur Probleme als ein Freund und ich die oberste Schicht komplett abgebaut hatten. Da gingen dann die FPS ziemlich runter, aber sobald man weiter unten war, haben sich diese wieder stabilisiert.
EDIT: In 2.0 musste ich die Grafik ordentlich runterschrauben, weil ich sonst ständig nur an die 30 FPS gehabt hätte, weil das Spiel so viele Ressourcen frisst.

Preis:
Ich habe damals 4,24€ dafür gezahlt. Auch den Vollpreis ist das Spiel wert da man doch ein paar Stunden was zu tun hat.

Spielzeit:
Da wir es zwei Mal durchspielen mussten, weil die Errungenschaft fürs durchspielen nur beim Host zählte, mussten wir uns nochmal schnell komplett durch alle Ebenen durchbuddeln damit ich die Errungenschaft auch bekomme. Also einer alleine braucht ca 4h und mit jemand zweitem braucht man dann ca 5h oder wie bei mir 4,8h.
EDIT: Für beide Versionen braucht man ca 13,5h.

Vergleich zum Vorgänger:
Den gibt es nicht. Es gibt nur so ähnliche Games. 

Errungenschaften:
Insgesamt gibt es 43 Errungenschaften und diese sind auch recht einfach mittels Guides zu erreichen. Diese zählen auch. Ich habe für 100% 4,8h gebraucht. Für Sammler ist das Spiel dadurch sehr zu empfehlen.
EDIT: Insgesamt gibt es nun durch 2.0 75 Errungenschaften und diese erreicht man insgesamt in 13,5h. Nur für 2.0 habe ich mit einem Freund 8,7h gebraucht.

Story:
Die gibt es nicht.

Gameplay:
Man gräbt sich simpel von oben nach ganz unten, upgradet verschiedene Dinge und beendet das Spiel dann auf der untersten Ebene. Upgraden kann man die Spitzhacke auf 20; den Rucksack auch; die Batterie hat auch 20 Upgrades, aber die Preise für die Energiewiederaufladung steigen stark und hängen nicht davon ab wie viel Energie man bereits verloren hat sondern sind immer ein fester Wert; das Jetpack hat auch 20 Upgrades und das Dynamit 5. Es gibt 7 Checkpoints beim Runtergraben damit man nicht immer ganz oben anfangen muss. Wenn die Batterie/Energie alle ist, dann verliert man den kompletten Loot und spawnt ganz oben wieder. Dort, wo man spawnt, gibt es einen Kleiderschrank zum Skin wechseln, einen Emote Shop für Ingameemotes gegen Ingamegeld, einen Händler für Sprühfarben und Idle-Arbeiter die man maximal auf 15 leveln kann durch ein Sammelitem, das man beim Buddeln finden kann. Diese buddeln und nach einer gewissen Zeit kann man dort Geld abholen. Fallschaden gibt es nicht. Bezüglich der Sammelitems gibt es mehrere. Wir haben 15 Items für die Arbeiterupgrades, Skins in Kisten, Dinosaurierteile, Teleportsteine, Batterien und Geldkisten. Wichtig für den Multiplayer: Loot wird geteilt. Also, wenn einer Materialien sammelt, dann verschwindet dieses beim anderen. Bei den Sammelitems weiß ich nicht mehr so genau was da geteilt wird und was nicht. Geldkisten wurden auf jeden Fall geteilt. Der Rest, glaube ich, nicht. Materialien an sich gibt es viele verschiedene mit unterschiedlichem Geldwert. Je weiter man nach unten kommt umso bessere findet man.
EDIT: Es gibt haufenweise Neuerungen in 2.0. Man kann nun Ausrüstung wie Sauger, Rucksack, Seil, Stiefel, Dynamit, Batterie und Scanner ausrüsten und man hat die Wahl ob man mit der Spitzhacke, der Schaufel oder dem Bohrer gräbt. Bei den 10 unterschiedlichen Erzen, die man zu Barren verarbeiten kann für die Blaupausen, haben wir sehr viele Stufen der Stärke der einzelnen Gegenstände. Noch dazu gibt es 5 Seltenheitsstufen (gewöhnlich, ungewöhnlich, selten, episch und legendär) und Qualitätsstufen von 0-100 die auch nochmal einen großen Einfluss auf die Items nehmen. Der Unterschied von Eisen (erste Ressource) zu dunkler Materie (letzter Ressource) ist immens in allen Belangen. Nun zu den Blaupausen. Wir finden in den 10 unterschiedlichen "Biomen" jeweils eine Truhenart die Blaupausen enthält die man wiederum mit Barren verwenden kann. Weiters gibt es nun einen Orbhändler bei dem man Edelsteine in Orbs umwandeln kann die auch noch Buffs in verschiedenen Bereichen geben. Ausrüsten kann man 4 Stück. Wir können auch die Lagerkiste 5x aufwerten und den Brennofen 3x. Die Grabtiefe beträgt nun sogar 5000m.

Fazit:
Mir hat das Spiel sehr viel Spaß gemacht da ich es mit einem guten Freund durchgezockt hatte. Alleine wäre es eher langweilig gewesen. Es erfindet das Rad jetzt auch nicht neu, aber für kurzweiligen Spaß mit Freunden ist es definitiv zu empfehlen. Die vielen Errungenschaften und die schnell erreichten 100% sind zwei weitere Punkte weshalb ich das Game nur positiv bewerten kann.
EDIT: Mir hat 2.0 sehr gut gefallen und das die Spielzeit nur etwas länger als die von 1.0 war, war genau richtig. Auch die ganzen Neuerungen wie Crafting fand ich eine deutliche Verbesserung zu Teil 1 und das alles auch noch gratis und man kann obendrein auswählen ob man 1.0 oder 2.0 zocken will. In welchem Spiel kann man das schon. Von mir bekommt es also weiterhin einen riesigen Daumen nach oben.

Ich wünsche euch noch viel Spaß beim Zocken und bis zur nächsten Rezension.

한국어 지원이 없다는 점이 처음엔 조금 아쉽게 느껴졌습니다. 하지만 막상 플레이를 시작하고 나서는 언어 장벽이 전혀 문제가 되지 않을 정도로 직관적이고, 무엇보다 게임 자체가 너무 재미있어서 금방 빠져들게 됩니다. 단순히 땅을 파는 게임이라고 생각하면 오산입니다. 이 게임은 자원 관리, 업그레이드, 전략적 선택, 그리고 끊임없는 도전 욕구를 자극하는 훌륭한 게임 디자인을 갖추고 있습니다.
특히 마음에 들었던 점은 밸런스입니다. 초반에는 누구나 쉽게 접근할 수 있도록 설계되어 있고, 후반부로 갈수록 점점 더 깊은 전략적 사고와 집중력이 요구되면서 성취감이 극대화됩니다. 업그레이드 시스템도 잘 짜여 있어서, 내가 직접 성장해 나간다는 느낌이 강하게 들고, 그 과정에서 오는 만족감이 큽니다.
그래픽과 사운드는 화려하지 않지만, 오히려 그 단순함이 게임의 본질적인 재미를 더 잘 살려줍니다. 불필요한 장식 없이 핵심에 집중하게 만들어 주는 디자인 덕분에 몰입도가 높습니다.

At first, the lack of Korean language support in Keep Digging felt a little disappointing. However, once I actually started playing, I realized that the language barrier is hardly an issue thanks to the game’s intuitive design—and more importantly, the gameplay itself is so engaging that I was quickly drawn in. It’s a mistake to think of this as just a simple digging game. In reality, it’s a well-crafted experience that combines resource management, upgrades, strategic choices, and a constant drive to push yourself further.

One of the aspects I appreciated most was the balance. The early stages are designed to be accessible to anyone, making it easy to get started. But as you progress, the game gradually demands deeper strategic thinking and sharper focus, which maximizes the sense of achievement. The upgrade system is also well thought out, giving you a strong feeling of personal growth and satisfaction as you advance.

The graphics and sound aren’t flashy, but that simplicity actually enhances the core fun of the game. By stripping away unnecessary decoration, the design keeps you focused on what really matters, which makes the immersion even stronger.

This game has been a total waste of time, and the game mechanics don't make sense. For example: dynamite should have a bigger explosive radius as you upgrade it and leave at least a bit more ores to the player. Second why would I want to scroll between a shovel and a pickaxe if i already upgraded it (if you are going to make this available, at least make it available to the other abilities as well). Third why would the whole city get nuked. Fourth there should have been animation, for that much a price tag come on. Fifth and my last complaint, you should've made the damn game free or at least early access. This game is not finished yet and will likely never be finished. Congrats developer team you are the ultimate digger!!!

Gameplay is ok... so here is my beef. You use dynamite, you would think dynamite would blow a hole and all this wonderful loot would fall at your feet, I mean after all the dynamite is 10k a pop. No, you get your hole, and all the loot that was hiding in the rock is destroyed. The other problem is when you hit terrain above you, the loot doesn't drop down, it hovers in air, so its not like you can just clear a big patch and let it all drop down and collect, nope you have to collect as you go. 

That's my review.

review:
このゲームを4.1時間ほどプレイした頃には「少し掘ってみよう」という軽い興味が「掘らないと落ち着かない」という状態へと徐々に変化して行きました。
序盤こそ目新しい鉱石や発見に楽しさを感じられるものの、次第に目をガンギマラせながら理性を地層に埋め、意思と石を無心で掘り続ける作業へと移行していき、朝起きて石を掘り、食事の合間に石を掘り、大学をさぼって石を掘り、夜になってもなお穴を掘り、風呂では今日の掘りを振り返ってから再び穴を掘るという、少し何かを間違えた日常を自然に受け入れさせられる不思議で素晴らしい体験を提供してくれます。
その結果、現実世界でもスコップやつるはしが妙に身近な存在となり、今では共同生活をしているかのような感覚すら覚え、一番の友達として夢にまで登場してくれるようになりました。
それほどまでに本作は「掘る」という単純な行為を通じてプレイヤーの思考や生活に静かに入り込み、馬鹿馬鹿しさの中に哲学的な余韻を残す、印象深いゲームだったと感じています。

J’ai joué à Keep Digging avec mon frère, et honnêtement, ce fut une excellente surprise du début à la fin. Nous avons terminé le jeu en environ 3h30, en prenant le temps d’explorer correctement, et nous avons obtenu 100 % des succès Steam, ce qui montre à quel point l’expérience est bien équilibrée et gratifiante.

Dès les premières minutes, le jeu pose une ambiance efficace. Le concept est simple sur le papier, mais extrêmement bien exécuté. Le gameplay repose sur une boucle claire et addictive : creuser, optimiser, progresser, puis recommencer avec de nouvelles possibilités. Chaque session donne envie d’aller “juste un peu plus loin”, et c’est là que Keep Digging réussit parfaitement son pari.

🎮 Gameplay

Le gameplay est fluide, intuitif et très bien rythmé. Les mécaniques sont faciles à comprendre, mais la progression ajoute progressivement de la profondeur sans jamais devenir lourde ou frustrante. On sent que tout a été pensé pour que le joueur reste engagé :

aucune mécanique inutile

aucune phase ennuyeuse

pas de temps mort artificiel

Le fait d’y jouer à deux (même en alternant ou en partageant l’expérience) renforce énormément le plaisir. On discute des choix, on compare les stratégies, et on se motive mutuellement à aller chercher tous les succès.

🏆 Succès Steam

Mention spéciale pour les succès Steam, qui sont intelligemment conçus. Ils ne demandent pas de grinding absurde ni d’actions contre-intuitives. Tous les succès encouragent à explorer l’intégralité du jeu et à comprendre ses mécaniques en profondeur. Obtenir le 100 % est un vrai plaisir, pas une corvée.

⏱️ Durée de vie

Environ 3h30 pour finir le jeu à 100 %, ce qui est selon moi parfait pour ce type d’expérience. Le jeu ne cherche pas à s’étirer artificiellement, et respecte totalement le temps du joueur. On termine l’aventure satisfait, avec le sentiment d’avoir vécu une expérience complète et maîtrisée.

🎨 Direction artistique & ambiance

Visuellement, le jeu est simple mais efficace. Le style colle parfaitement au concept, la lisibilité est excellente, et l’ambiance sonore accompagne très bien l’action sans jamais devenir répétitive ou envahissante.

✅ Points positifs

✔ Gameplay addictif et bien équilibré
✔ Progression claire et gratifiante
✔ Excellente conception des succès Steam
✔ Parfait à jouer et partager avec un proche
✔ Durée de vie maîtrisée, sans remplissage inutile

❌ Points négatifs

Honnêtement, il est difficile de trouver de vrais défauts. On pourrait éventuellement regretter que l’expérience ne dure pas un peu plus longtemps… mais c’est presque un compliment, tant le jeu est agréable.

🔥 Conclusion

Keep Digging est un excellent jeu, fun, intelligent et très bien conçu. Il sait exactement ce qu’il veut être, et il le fait à la perfection. Une expérience idéale à partager, satisfaisante à compléter à 100 %, et que je recommande sans la moindre hésitation.

👉 Recommandé à 100 % 👍

追記：ver2.0をちょっとプレイしてみての感想
コントローラー対応してくれたのは良かったと思います。しかしアイテム欄での操作、インゴット作成の際の鉱石の移動などはマウスの方がやりやすくて結局二刀流です。大谷翔平です。
あとはver1.0と比べて掘り進みづらくなった気がします。プレイヤーのシャベルを振るう速度が遅くなって爽快感が減りました。筋肉も減りました。逆にドリルが非常に楽しいです。文明の利器には敵いません。
追加要素としてオーブ生成がありました。レアそうな鉱石を集めて装備できるアクセサリみたいなものを作れるようになりました。あんまり進めてませんがこれいる？掘りゲーなのに要素盛り盛りでプラマイゼロです。
最後に掘ったあとのほったらかし鉱石を掃除機で吸って回収できるようになりました。ですが目の前にあっても吸わないときがあります。吸引力が変わるただひとつの掃除機です。



まだありました、落下死が追加されました。これについては縦に掘り進むだけのver1.0の改善で導入されたものみたいですが、ちょっと悲しいです。フレンドリーファイアも追加されて体力の制限が大幅に増えた気がします。これいる？フレンドリーファイアだけはほんまにいらない気がします。

結論！　　１０点中４点です。追加要素が多すぎて単純に穴を掘る作業に没頭するのが難しいかもしれません。

I am a chimpanzee and I am digging a hole.

*Spoiler Warning*
In Keep Digging, the transition from a hot and burly construction man to unhinged primate is exactly what the gaming space needs more of. While everyone starts as a standard customisable human, the game quickly leans into monkey business as both a cosmetic choice and a gameplay mechanic. As you descend toward the 1,000 metre mark, you unlock various chimpanzee skins that replace your standard character model. This isn't just a visual change: it's a lifestyle. There is something deeply fulfilling about watching a primate finally pulling their weight on this planet and doing the menial jobs for us. If only real chimpanzee's could follow in their footsteps.

The game also features specific emotes for the chimpanzee, allowing you to fully commit to your new lifestyle. When you aren't digging, you can stand at the edge of your hole and perform grunts at your friends or better yet flip them off.
Deep underground you'll find plenty of mine shafts, chambers, cathedrals and OMG they're worshipping the chimpanzee.

Playing as a chimpanzee provides a phsychological edge. When a human digs a 500 metre hole, it looks like a labour violation: when a chimpanzee does it, it looks like a visionary pursuing his dreams. Chimpanzees taking the next leap into evolution.
Darwin would be proud.

[h3]Keep Digging is the debut title from Wild Dog, and while it serves as a decent "hello world" for a small two-person team, it struggles to justify even its modest $5 price tag.[/h3]

The premise is exactly what it says on the tin: you start on a plot of land confined by a concrete box and dig down. You collect ore, sell it for upgrades, and repeat the loop until you reach the bottom of the map.

However, the game has almost zero standalone value. The sound design is negligible, the story is non-existent, and the gameplay loop becomes monotonous within minutes. If you play this solo, you are essentially just clicking on dirt in silence.

The only redemption lies in the multiplayer. Like many "friend slop" games, the fun doesn't come from the mechanics, but from the chaos of dragging your friends into a pit. The goofy emotes and the ability to mess with your teammates can carry the experience for a single evening of laughter.

If you and a group of friends have absolutely nothing else to play and $5 burning a hole in your pocket, you might get two hours of entertainment out of this. For everyone else, keep your money and more importantly, your time for something with a bit more soul.

[b]TLDR[/b]
Keep Digging is standard-issue "friendslop" in a sea of better co-op games. It has no value as a solo experience, and while the goofy physics might get a laugh out of your friend group for one night, the novelty wears off the moment you close the game.

[b]4.5/10[/b]

---- 以下は、ネタバレを含む。----

[spoiler]
序盤の終わり辺りからファースト・トラベルのマンホールの設置される深さ(間隔)が大きく開いてくるので、恐らく鉱石を稼いでレベリングして欲しいという事なのだろう。ここでダレる。
このゲーム、バッテリー切れで自動的に全回復する乾電池と、一気に地上へ戻れるワープストーンと呼ばれる物があるのだが、これが販売されておらずに出土するのを待つしか無い。しかも、一度クリアするとマップは初期化できても発掘されたものはそのままなので補充することがほぼできない。・・・マルチプレイで他のサーバーでプレイすれば出土して持ち帰ることができるのだろうが、ソロだとそう言った稼ぎができない。

どういう事かというと、回復アイテムがないので、次のファースト・トラベルの深度まで一気に進むしか無くなる。時間をかけてジックリとプレイするのでなければ、基本的に「直下堀り」という垂直にひたすら掘り進めるというプレイスタイルしか確立できなかったりする。無駄が無いプレイ方法かも知れないが、探索もへったくれも無い。鉱石がたくさん出土するのはいいけど、インベントリーが狭いから直下堀り中の鉱石は回収できないものがほとんどとなる。だから、鉱石が邪魔になると直下堀も面倒くさい。鉱石がマウスポインターのフォーカスを奪うので、真下に掘り進められないことが多くなる。
・・・なので、スキルが低い序盤は200m～400mが山場だ。それ以降は途中で深い空洞に落ちていくと戻る術を失ってしまうので、必然的にそのまま次のファースト・トラベルの深度まで一気に行くしか選択肢が無くなる。深度100m毎のファースト・トラベルでも良い気がするのだが…やはりマルチ前提のスタイルなのかな。

あと、個人的にエンディングで掘り進めた穴を蟻の巣を観察するように透過して見せてくれるのだが、この状態を保存できるようにして鑑賞（またはオンライン公開）できるようにした方が面白かったかなあと思う。
強くてニューゲームもいいけど、十数時間かけて掘り抜いたルートは芸術作品(っぽいと思うよ充分に)として残せた方が良かったとも思う。同じ物はほぼ作れないと思うからね。そこはとても残念だった。

Digging Game delivers exactly what it promises: you dig a hole, often with friends, and for a few hours you'll have some laughs. At a low price point, it's a passable diversion that doesn't oversell itself, but its potential doesn't go much further than the initial novelty.

The core gameplay loop is straightforward—pick a direction, dig dirt, collect ore, sell it, and repeat. It's easy to break through the game by simply digging straight down, which the developers have publicly addressed as a known issue. For now, don't expect any meaningful challenge or exploration beyond the linear path of least resistance.

If you do stick around longer, the lack of depth becomes apparent. Replayability is limited; once you've tunneled through the content, you've seen everything on offer. The game doesn't introduce new surprises or fresh objectives, and most players report getting their fill within 2 to 5 hours. The only way to stretch that time is bringing friends, as multiplayer can turn digging into a bit more of a spectacle, though all important actions are locked to the host, which can be frustrating.

A bigger issue lies in the technical polish. Even players with high-end hardware report constant lag and performance drops, regardless of settings. Crashes and disconnects are common, and Linux users are out of luck entirely with the game's lack of Proton compatibility. There are also some visual bugs, like odd geometry and digging artifacts, which detract from the experience.

The resource system could use some balancing. Ore is everywhere—so much so that mining starts to feel like an inventory management chore rather than a satisfying discovery. There's needless tedium in hauling ore back and forth, especially since the carrying capacity is tiny and you can't even sprint.

Despite all that, for the few dollars it costs, if you're after a quick, mindless co-op game to kill an evening with friends, this will deliver for a short burst. But unless the developers seriously overhaul the core mechanics, progression, and technical stability, don't expect to keep coming back. Dig your hole, have your laughs, and move on to the next game.

* There is SO MUCH ore that it's a huge bottleneck. * There are gaps in the voxel geometry and I've already seen weird triangles and artifacts that I can't dig away.

This game is rather fun. For a $5 game, it's worth it. Fun game to just waste some time on. 

HOWEVER there are issues I'd like to address (mainly in hopes the devs see this and can fix/ change them):

First off, playing with friends is very fun, but as you progress through the game, you find bones (I wont say too much more that isn't in the trailer). Only the host can pick these bones up, this part I'm ok with, but if you're playing with friends, the friend doesn't get the final achievement from the bones, and cannot see the finished skeleton. I feel like it would be nice for guests to also see the skeleton, as well as get the achievement.
Additionally, while progressing through the game, you unlock workers to produce resources for you. The host can collect the money produced, and the money is given to all players, BUT the guests cannot collect this. I feel like, if the money goes to everyone, let everyone collect it.

Next, you can find chests and other goodies while exploring. If the host picks these items up first, the guest cannot pick them up, but if the guest picks them up first, the host can. I feel like it should be consistent, either only 1 person can pick it up, or more ideally, just make it to where the host can pick up, and so can the guest, no matter who picks up first.

There is no run. There's no form of running, sprinting, nothing. I feel like this game could use sprinting for all the back and forth running you will be doing.
To go along with this idea, I feel like keybinds should be added to change the run button, as well as re-map other buttons for accessibility reasons. (I personally hate the fact that the wire rope button is shift, and I constantly use it mistakenly when I try to run, as shift is the primary run button in most other games). Also being able to press 'ESC' to escape UIs would be nice... I'm just too lazy to want to press the red 'X' in each UI.

While digging, you might get the urge to just dig straight down, which is a completely valid option in this game, BUT once your backpack gets full, you are no longer able to dig easily because the ores just get in the way. I propose a few changes; make the ores un-selectable/highlightable when the backpack is full, or just break the ores. Delete them. That's it.
To go along with this, you may want to collect specific items, so I feel like being able to open your backpack with a keybind might be a good idea as well, and possibly even select an item to be able to delete them from your backpack to make space for more valuable items.
Additionally I feel like this game would be cool to have some kind of collectable screen that will showcase all the different ores you've collected including all the "Huge" or "Massive" ores, that way it's easier to identify which ores you're missing for achievements.
Which brings me to my final idea; Very small change, renaming the "Huge" or "Massive" ores to just "Giant" ores just to match the "Gettin' Jiggy wit Dem Ores" achievement. My girlfriend and I were playing this and assumed there were specific 1-time collectable "Giant Ores" hidden around the map that we needed to find and collect, until she accidently got the achievement. I just think this one would alleviate some confusion.

Additionally, I feel like it could use a bit of another optimization update. My girlfriend doesn't run a terribly computer, but was forced to lower all graphics to minimum because she kept getting massive lag spikes.

Again, don't get me wrong, this game is just relaxing, dumb fun, but it could use a little bit more polish. 8/10 would recommend.

Keep Digging, developed and published by Wild Dog, is a cooperative sandbox game that transforms the simple act of digging into a social and strangely satisfying experience. It takes a humble concept—burrowing into the earth in search of resources—and turns it into a meditative rhythm of teamwork, exploration, and steady progression. Rather than relying on combat or survival tension, the game builds its appeal around the tactile pleasure of discovery and the camaraderie that forms as players chip away at the underground world together. It’s a title that thrives on simplicity, asking little of its players beyond patience, cooperation, and a curiosity to see what lies beneath the surface.

At its core, Keep Digging is about descent. Players begin at ground level, equipped with basic tools and limited stamina, and are tasked with digging deeper and deeper—up to a staggering 1,000 meters below the surface. Each layer of the subterranean world reveals new materials, from common dirt and stone to rare minerals and hidden treasures buried within the depths. The structure is straightforward: gather resources, sell or trade them, use the profits to upgrade your tools, and then dig even further. The appeal lies in this feedback loop—each dig feels productive, each upgrade meaningful, and every layer conquered a step closer to mastery. The progression is steady and unhurried, making it a game that’s less about speed or competition and more about gradual satisfaction.

One of the game’s most notable features is its focus on cooperation. Up to eight players can dig together, sharing tools, discoveries, and strategies as they tunnel through the underground. This multiplayer design adds a social dimension that transforms what could have been a solitary routine into a lively, collaborative adventure. Communication becomes essential when coordinating digging directions, managing resources, or deciding which upgrades to prioritize. It’s this sense of teamwork that gives the game its charm—players develop a shared rhythm, carving tunnels together and laughing over missteps as they accidentally collapse tunnels or uncover unexpected pockets of valuable ore. The absence of combat or enemies makes the experience friendly and stress-free, emphasizing relaxation and creativity over tension or danger.

The upgrade system provides a sense of tangible progression that keeps the gameplay loop engaging. As players dig and collect resources, they earn the means to improve their equipment—stronger drills, better lighting, faster digging tools, or dynamite to blast through harder rock. Each new upgrade allows for deeper exploration, creating a satisfying feeling of empowerment as previously unreachable areas open up. The incremental nature of these enhancements encourages players to keep going, always looking for the next valuable vein or hidden relic. The simplicity of this system makes it easy to grasp, but the pacing ensures that each improvement feels earned, especially when shared among a team of players who have worked together to achieve it.

Visually, Keep Digging adopts a clean and functional art style that supports its underground theme without unnecessary embellishment. The layers of terrain are distinct and easy to read, helping players navigate and plan their tunnels effectively. Lighting plays an important role—descending deeper means darker environments, forcing players to rely on torches, headlamps, and creative lighting solutions to continue safely. The world is vibrant yet restrained, offering just enough visual variation to make each new layer feel distinct without overwhelming the senses. The minimalist aesthetic enhances the meditative quality of the experience, reinforcing the game’s rhythm of repetition and reward.

The sound design complements this atmosphere perfectly. The audio landscape is built from soft ambient tones, the echo of pickaxes striking rock, and the muffled hum of underground activity. The soundtrack, though subtle, adds warmth and tranquility to the experience, turning what could have been monotonous work into something almost therapeutic. In multiplayer sessions, the gentle background noise of digging often gives way to bursts of laughter or shouts of excitement as players make discoveries together. It’s a game that encourages relaxation while still rewarding attentiveness, using sound and motion to draw players into its hypnotic loop.

Despite its strengths, Keep Digging is not without its flaws. As with many indie titles centered on a single mechanic, the gameplay can feel repetitive after extended play. The lack of danger or challenge may cause some players to lose motivation once the novelty of digging wears off. While the cooperative aspect adds longevity, solo players might find the experience less compelling, as much of the charm depends on shared interaction. Technical limitations also appear in places—occasional synchronization issues in multiplayer sessions and performance dips during heavy activity remind players that this is a smaller-scale production. However, these issues are minor in the larger context of the game’s ambition, and the developers have shown active engagement with the community in patching and refining the experience.

Where Keep Digging truly succeeds is in how it captures the joy of steady progress and the pleasure of shared discovery. It’s a game that doesn’t demand constant attention but instead rewards consistency and cooperation. The absence of enemies, timers, or failure states allows players to play at their own pace, making it ideal for those who prefer a calm, social gaming experience rather than competitive or high-stress gameplay. It embodies the spirit of collaboration—the satisfaction of seeing a vast, hand-carved tunnel stretch beneath the earth, knowing it was the result of collective effort.

In the end, Keep Digging is a charming and contemplative cooperative experience that transforms a simple mechanic into something deeply engaging through atmosphere, teamwork, and steady progression. It doesn’t attempt to dazzle with complexity or spectacle but instead delivers a consistent sense of satisfaction through its tactile gameplay and social design. Whether played with friends for hours or enjoyed solo in shorter bursts, it offers a relaxing break from the intensity of most modern games. It’s a reminder that sometimes, the act of working together—digging a little deeper, one layer at a time—is rewarding enough on its own.

J’ai sauté sur le jeu avec un pote et franchement je ne m’attendais pas à autant de plaisir « simple et efficace ». Le concept est tout bête, on descend dans un monde souterrain, on creuse, on ramasse des trésors, on améliore ses outils, et on recommence. Là où ça marche, c’est que ça ne cherche pas à être plus que ce qu’il est, c’est relax, fun et coopératif à fond. On peut jouer jusqu’à 8 donc c’est idéal pour passer du bon temps.

La boucle est simple mais addictive, creuser -> récupérer -> vendre -> upgrader. Il y a une vraie satisfaction à voir ta pelle devenir une machine de destruction massive de roches. Les visuels ne sont pas ultra-fou, mais assez propres, l’ambiance dans les sous terrains est chouette aussi. Jouer à plusieurs change tout, tu peux délirer librement sans te prendre la tête et ça devient une vraie session « on creuse jusqu’à plus soif ». 
Pas besoin d’être un pro, la prise en main est rapide, c’est assez accessible et si tu veux juste te poser, jouer tranquillement avec une musique en fond et creuser pendant une heure, ça passe nickel. Ça fait du bien.

J’ai poussé le délire jusqu’au 100%, trouver tous les objets, tout améliorer, tout explorer… y’a une vraie satisfaction à tout cocher. C’est pas un 100% qu’on fait juste pour les succès, c’est un 100% que t’as envie de faire, juste parce que le jeu est chill et te garde accroché.

Bien sûr, ce n’est pas parfait, certains joueurs pointent du doigt une fin un peu rapide, ou des soucis de contenu/optimisation à régler. Mais honnêtement, pour le prix et ce que ça propose, je trouve que ça vaut largement le coup.

En résumé, si tu aimes les jeux où tu peux te poser, creuser, découvrir des coffres, mettre à jour ton matos et rigoler avec des potes, Keep Digging est un coup de cœur assuré. Un jeu qui ne se la pète pas, mais qui remplit parfaitement son rôle.

Et maintenant, à force d’y jouer j’ai pris un réflexe bizarre, dès que je vois un tas de gravats dans la vraie vie, j’ai envie de sortir une pioche. Bizarre, non ?

装備強化の進捗スピードもちょうどいい塩梅でストレス無く遊べました。戦闘等のシステムは一切無く本当にただ掘るだけのゲームなので、ルートを考えてコツコツ掘るもヨシ、特定深度にあるファストトラベル地点やスタート地点へのワープアイテム等を頼りにしたパワープレイもヨシ、お好きな方法で自由に掘り進めていくのが楽しいと思います。道中にはスキン等が入った宝箱等の収集要素もあり、それも良い感じにゲームプレイを飽きさせない要素になっていると思います。

最大8人までのマルチプレイも可能で、自分も実際4人でのマルチプレイを一度遊びましたが、自分はどちらかというとソロ向きのゲームかなと思いました。収集要素もあるし、ひとりでコツコツ好きなように掘る方が楽しいと感じたのがその理由ですが、この辺はまぁ人による感じだと思います。マルチプレイは無いよりはあった方が絶対良いですし。

そして最後に自分の総評ですが、採掘ゲーが好きな方なら値段以上に楽しめる良ゲーだと思います。オススメです。

前述のようにver.1が凄く楽しめたし、実績も追加されてるようなので「またやるか！」と思いver.2もプレイ。と、思ったら３D酔いが酷過ぎてすぐ辞めてしまいました。実績全解除はしたいと思い何度かプレイ開始しましたが、30分の継続プレイも無理なレベルで酔ってしまい諦めました。
おそらくですが縦に掘るのに適した装備というものがあるので、掘削力に縦と横の概念が入って掘った時のグラフィックの処理が違うのと、それも原因となって昇る時に引っ掛かりまくって画面が揺れるのが主な要因かなと思います。

なので自分としてはゲーム内容を語る以前の問題なのですが、UIもお世辞にも出来がいいとは言い難く、追加された要素もぱっと見では煩わしさの方が勝る印象です。
しかも先程もう一度ゲームを開始したら、チェストの中のアイテムが全部消えて装備が初期の石のショベルに戻っていましたので、もう本当に二度とプレイすることは無いと思います。

ということで評価もオススメしないに変更しておきますが、ver.1は凄く楽しめましたので、実績全解除等を気にしない人であればver.1のプレイはオススメです。

Keep Digging: A Profoundly excellent game 🐵

Keep Digging is a masterclass in minimalist design, proving that profound depth can be found in the simple act of digging straight down. It strips away complex crafting and sprawling worlds, focusing entirely on a compelling loop of digging, reward, and resource management. With every descent, the game becomes a test of greed versus prudence: do you push further for a bigger haul, or ascend to upgrade your persistent shovel? This delightfully addictive experience is an absolute gem for those who appreciate a single, perfectly executed mechanic: Digging Straight Down.
멀티 말곤 특별한 장점이 하나도 없는 게임인데 싱글로 연습만 해보고 정작 중요한 멀티는 오류 때문에 하질못함

---

這不僅僅是一款挖礦遊戲，更像是一次深入地球脈絡與人類工業亡魂的考古之旅。《挖！挖！挖！》以19世紀工業革命為背景，將玩家拋入一個充滿黑煤、鐵鏽與血汗的深淵。你並非普通的礦工，而是歷史洪流中的一粒塵埃，在機械的轟鳴與地殼的震顫中，試圖從大地臟腑中榨取財富，卻意外撕開了時空的裂縫，驚醒了沈睡千萬年的遠古噩夢——一具被貪婪與火藥喚醒的霸王龍化石巨獸。

遊戲的核心機制堪稱魔鬼級的硬核體驗。前期，你需通過真實的歷史科技樹升級裝備：從簡陋的蒸汽鑽機到硝化炸藥，每一樣工具都對應著19世紀礦業技術的重大突破。礦層結構基於真實地質年代設計，二疊紀的煤層中藏著蕨類植物化石，白堊紀的岩層中則暗藏恐龍骨骼碎片。這些並非單純的收集品，而是解鎖霸王龍弱點的唯一線索。例如，只有通過分析化石分布，才能發現霸王龍對特定頻率的震動敏感，或其眼眶骨骼存在舊傷——這些細節均基於古生物學研究還原。

而真正的震撼在於BOSS戰的設計。霸王龍不僅是血厚攻高的怪物，更是自然力量的化身。它的每一次衝鋒都伴隨著地層塌陷，咆哮聲混合著19世紀工廠的汽笛噪音，彷彿工業革命的亡魂與遠古霸主的怒吼共振。戰鬥失敗後，遊戲會生成一份“歷史事件報告”，對比真實礦業災難（如1887年英國煤礦爆炸）與玩家死亡原因，迫使你反思：人類對資源的掠奪是否必然伴隨毀滅？

遊戲中最深刻的隱喻埋藏在結局分支中：若選擇用炸藥徹底毀滅霸王龍，會觸發“殖民擴張”結局——礦場擴張至全球，但世界淪為機械荒漠；若選擇用聲學裝置將其催眠回地層，則解鎖“生態平衡”結局——礦業技術轉型，人類與自然達成脆弱和解。這些選擇直指工業史的核心矛盾：進步是否必須踐踏過去？

《挖！挖！挖！》用鎬與火藥的碰撞，敲響了歷史的回聲。它告訴你：挖礦不只是挖礦，而是挖出人類貪婪的化石；打BOSS也不只是戰鬥，而是與整個文明史的陰影對決。如果你願意直面地層之下的血與鐵，這將是一場300小時都難以釋懷的旅程。

There's nothing wrong with that, but at least buy and add assets that fit your game.

Why am I compiling 900+ shaders for a game about digging? Appears to be made by an amateur developer with a lot to learn. This is not a performant game. The amount of bloom and graphic settings you cannot turn off is absurdly annoying. My friend kept lagging the further we were digging and on my high-end rig I noticed for such a simple concept it's not the best optimized game.

We didn't have the best time in Keep Digging. Cheap game, but that's exactly what you're buying: a cheaply made game. I could get passed a lot of the annoyances, but holy moly do some optimizations. When they have responses to feedback about optimizations it doesn't give me hope with this game at all. Hard Pass.

The game was honestly fun, but I’d never play this one solo. It’s definitely something that’s way more enjoyable with a friend. My friend and I finished the main game in about 2 hours, and then it took us another 12 ish hours to get all 100 achievements. Despite its flaws, we actually had a good time.

Gameplay & Content:

Keep Digging feels like a quick project.. something put together in Unity using pre-made assets. It doesn’t have much of a cohesive identity beyond “What if we made Digging a Hole, but multiplayer?” There’s no randomization in the levels, so every full playthrough feels exactly the same. Once you’ve done everything once, there’s really no reason to replay it.

That said, if you just want a silly, mindless game to play with friends for a night (especially on sale), it’s worth grabbing for a laugh.

Issues:
The game can be a bit laggy at times
Constant “shaders compiling” every time the game loads.. a huge annoyance
Menus feel clunky (pressing ESC doesn’t properly close them)
No sprinting, which really hurts the pacing
The overall design feels inconsistent and unpolished
Achievement Problem (Important):

*UPDATE*
I recently reinstalled the game because I saw new achievements were added (I’m an achievement hunter and wanted to max out the badge), only to find that the achievements are currently bugged.

It shows that I don’t have everything unlocked anymore, even though I previously completed all achievements. Some of the new ones also appear as placeholder names (like “NEW_ACHIEVEMENT_NAME”), which makes it seem like they aren’t fully implemented or released properly.

This is really frustrating, especially for completionists. It’s unclear whether this is a bug or unfinished content that was accidentally pushed live, but it definitely needs to be fixed.

Final Thoughts:

Keep Digging needs more polish to be on the same level as Digging a Hole. I’ll happily revise this review once a few updates drop and the game gets refined, but right now, it’s hard to genuinely recommend unless you’re just looking for a fun, short co-op experience to mess around with...

What is good:
・ I see how pricing might be reasonable for many for the fun of the few hours, maybe a day or two if you create a challenge for yourself like I did to dig as much as possible until you are bored

Why dislike:
・Too long loading time for such a small game, many bigger AAA games loads 10 times faster, no joke here
・Loading performance: if you read the performance update it says that the big change is that they put a 80% CPU limit to their already problematic code and called it a performance update. As a developer myself this is miserable. I suspect that everything runs on a single main thread what is their code and not the engine which is just bad.
・Playtime performance: I played it on a gaming laptop, it is not the newest or the best but still many AAA games runs without any issue and this little game just lags, it is not normal at all.
・Bugs: you can clip and fall through terrain, ores are not persistent in saves (they disappear), grass floating in the air after loading a save, unbreakable or hardly breakable little patches floating in the air, breakable entities outside of limits on the other side of the wall, I am not sure if the smoothness that the color spray creates is feature because it was intended to or because it is bug which was labeled as a feature, you push your pickaxe to brake instead of a minimal swing animation, it is like you want to push a button with the pickaxes head, and the list continues

Why the dislike if I played 19 hours anyway:
Games should not be cheap because they are full of bugs, have major performance issues and its creator is clearly not a real developer and watched some basic tutorials on youtube and felt like he could squeeze some money out of it. As a developer I would not encourage that with a like. A game should be cheap when it is small but it is operating reasonably well within its own limits.

永遠の謎ですね。
穴を掘る ⇒ 鉱石を持ち帰り売る ⇒ 装備を強化する ⇒ 穴を掘る を繰り返す作業ゲー。
ソロで綺麗に整地する、マルチでバカ騒ぎしながら掘る、どちらの遊び方もできます。

最大深度は現状1,000m。
直下掘りもできますが、深くなるほど地質・鉱石が固くなっていくので、
基本的には装備を強化しつつ緩やかに掘り下げていくのがスムーズでしょう。
一定の深度ごとにファストトラベルポイントもあります。

恐竜の化石収集、労働者（オートで稼いでくれるBOT）のレベルアップ、地下に眠る謎の遺構・施設など、
掘削作業のちょっとしたアクセントもあります。特に遺構・施設は謎が深まります。
また一部の衣服（というかアバター？）は周回要素です。
周回は強くてニューゲーム状態なので二回目以降はあっという間に最大深度まで辿り着けるでしょう。
実績周りも作業していれば直ぐに全解除できるので実績集め大好きな人も安心です。

さらなる深度や遺構・施設の謎が分かるアプデがあったらいいなぁとは思いますが、
お値段的にはワンタイムのネタゲームという感じかもしれません。

[h1]ありふれた穴掘りゲームに埋もれる印象[/h1]
　本作の基本的な流れは「鉱石を掘って売却し、装備を強化する」という、よくある穴掘りゲームのサイクルです。登場する鉱石も石炭や銅、銀、金といった定番のラインナップで、目新しさを感じる部分はあまりありませんでした。更に強化項目も採掘範囲やエネルギー量の拡張といった馴染み深いものが中心で、どうしても既視感が強くなってしまいます。宝箱や化石といったコレクティブ要素も存在しますが、報酬やコレクション対象が変わっただけに留まっており、全体的には「他で見たことがある流れ」に感じました。

[h2]3D穴掘りでマルチ対応という特徴[/h2]
　一方で、他の同系統の作品と比べたときに目立つ特徴として「3D穴掘りゲームでのマルチ対応」が挙げられます。2D穴掘りゲームのマルチ対応作品は既にいくつかプレイしていましたが、3D穴掘りでフレンドと遊べるというのは、それだけで新鮮に感じられました。実際に遊んでみると、真面目に掘り進めるだけでなく、変わったスキンや小さなギャグ要素を共有して笑い合える場面もあり、ソロでは得られない楽しさがありました。フレンドと気軽に遊ぶタイトルとしては、十分に価値があると思います。

[h2]コンテンツの薄さと消化の早さ[/h2]
　地下で宝箱を発見すると、地上での自動資金生産の効率が上がる仕組みがあります。ただ、正直に言えばこの要素が必要になるほどゲームの難易度が高くなく、むしろ全体的にサクサク進んでしまう印象でした(特にマルチプレイだからこそ簡単に感じた部分もあるかもしれません)。また、宝箱から解放できるスキンやエモートもありますが、ゲーム自体の寿命が短いため、それらがやり込み要素や達成感に繋がることはあまりなく、寧ろ「そこにリソースを割く必要はあったのか...」と疑問に思ってしまいます。結果として、遊んでいる間はそういったスキンなどで一瞬の楽しさがあっても、全体的なゲームとしての厚みには欠ける印象でした。

　全体的には「穴掘りゲームのテンプレートを3Dでマルチ対応化した作品」という印象が強いですが、気軽にフレンドと遊ぶゲームとしてなら十分におすすめできる作品だと感じました。

Man kennt das: Die meisten Spiele schicken einen auf epische Abenteuer. Drachen erschlagen, Königreiche retten, Helden Epen schreiben. Dieses Spiel? Nein. Hier heißt es: Schaufel in die Hand und runter geht’s.

Ich habe schon viele Höhen in Spielen erlebt – aber selten so viele Tiefen. Wort Wörtlich. Es gibt keine Quests, keine großen Geschichten… außer die, die man sich selbst erzählt, während man überlegt: "Warum grabe ich eigentlich immer noch? "Was ist mein Leben?“

Das Spielgefühl ist eine Mischung aus Zen-Meditation und Arbeitslager. Jeder Klick bringt mich tiefer – psychologisch wie auch geologisch. Während andere Spiele einen belohnen, wenn man aufsteigt, bestraft dieses Spiel jede Ambition: Denn es geht nur runter.

Die Highlights?

1. Man findet Steine. Viele Steine. Verschiedene Steine. Ich habe mittlerweile mehr Ahnung von Sedimentschichten als jeder Hobby-Geologe.
2. Irgendwann kommt man auf die glorreiche Idee: „Was, wenn ich einfach nach oben gehe?“ Spoiler: Geht nicht. Das Spiel heißt nicht „Nach oben laufen“, sondern „Nach unten graben“.
3. Der Soundtrack klingt, als hätte jemand mit einem Eimer und einem Löffel eine Karriere gestartet. Absolut immersiv.

Fazit:
Dieses Spiel ist wie ein schlechter Witz – man lacht am Anfang, gräbt weiter, und irgendwann stellt man fest, dass der Witz auf Kosten der eigenen Freizeit geht. Aber genau darin liegt der Charme: Man hört einfach nicht auf.

Empfehlung?
Definitiv ja – für alle, die Minecraft spielen wollten, aber zu faul für Häuserbau und Craften sind.

I purchased this game for myself and my partner after seeing a YouTube video on the game. I thought it would be nice to play a digging game like this cooperatively.

I found, like others, that the game could be very easily completed linearly, with very little actual underground exploration. In my first playthrough, I dug straight down from the x until the first fast travel spot, then dug down from those, and seemed to dig through every cavern. This could have been fine, if there were different variants of exploration landmarks. As it is, you play it once and you've seen everything the game has to offer, then maybe do a second playthrough to finish collecting achievements.

However, upon attempting to play the game cooperatively issues arose. Firstly, money isn't shared, as suggested by the description of the game, but you don't realise how bad it feels for a coop game of this nature until you actually experience it. I at this point had all upgrades and achievements, which were carried with me to my partner's world, and was just playing with my partner for fun. That meant that my partner needed the value from the ores in order to purchase upgrades, while I did not. If the money was shared, ores I sold could have also gone towards this endeavour, which would have meant I could also pick up the ores.

Upgrades carrying over was not too bad, especially since the shovel levels could be cycled through with the scroll wheel, meaning I could keep the same shovel level as my partner throughout. However, I would argue the best way for the upgrades to be done would be each player having different upgrade levels dependant on the world they are currently in. This would allow for interesting money management gameplay, especially with a shared pool of money, as each player would still need to upgrade their own individual gear. It would also mean that all players in a world would be at the same point of progression.

All fast travel points unlocked on your "home world" also carry over to any world you visit. This is a massive problem when playing cooperatively, since if one player has gotten to the final fast travel spot, they can just teleport to the bottom and dig for the most valuable ores down there. Alternatively, they could just press the button and beat the game. I haven't yet tested if this would retain the 1000m fast travel spot for the visiting player, but given the other issues stated, I would hypothesise that the fast travel spot would be retained, which could result in beating the game multiple times in minutes.

The biggest issue we had while playing was that we would regularly clip through the floor, often by digging and sometimes even just walking. This caused us to fall down to the next open cavern below us. In some circumstances, the next open cavern was the bottom of the world. I'm unsure if this was a problem with cooperative play or something related to performance, but I would expect the floor to remain solid regardless of any potential performance issues. At times, my partner would also see the ground on the surface vanish visually, but I theorise this was likely a performance issue.

I hope that in time these issues will be resolved. However, until then, I cannot fully recommend this game to all potential players.

Вот что бы я улучшил:
1. Дать возможность зажимать мышку для копания, а не делать кликами это, а то превращается игра в кликер.
2. Динамит плохой, он на 3 уровне копает меньше чем кирка первоначальная, плюс взрывает руду, хз вообще зачем он нужен. 
3. Любую породу можно копать самой слабой киркой, просто это будет чуть дольше, надо было сделать чтобы условно как в майнкрафте, что некоторую породу кирка слабая вообще не берет, тогда бы игра проходилась дольше чем за полтора часа.
4. Сундуки надо синхронизировать между игроками, потому что кто-то что-то открыл непонятно где, забыл сказать и ты в итоге без сундука. Либо добавить возможность ставить метки.
5. Надо точно добавить метки игроков других, чтобы было понятно где кто.
6. Хз че дается за прохождение игры, мне за одно прохождение дали продавца руды, за второе продавца балончиков с краской. При этом они у меня и так с самого начала были открыты. 
7. С юай надо работать, шрифты выезжают за кнопки.

[h1] Recenze: Keep Digging[/h1]
[h1] ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️[/h1]

Pokud jste vždycky chtěli kopat tunel do centra Země, ale báli jste se, že vás při tom odvede policie nebo vyhodí sousedi, Keep Digging je pro vás ideální terapie.

Za nějakých 5 hodin jsem nejen dosáhl dna (doslova 1000 metrů), ale i 100 % achievementů – což je mimochodem nejpříjemnější „platinovka“, jakou jsem kdy měl. Žádné nervy, žádné souboje, žádné stealth mise, kde vás vyřadí jeden nedomyšlený krok. Jenom já, lopata, dynamit… a občas banda kamarádů, kteří místo kopání malují barevným sprejem po zdech jako podzemní Banksy.

Hra je přesně to, co slibuje – pohodová oddychovka. Žádné „git gud“, žádné „tryhard“, jen čisté zenové kopání, prodávání nálezů a vylepšování vybavení. A že i lopata umí být cool na levelu 20, to byste nevěřili. NPC pomocníci makají, i když vy spíte, takže máte skoro pocit, že jste si pořídili digitální brigádníky.

Multiplayer je parádní – až 8 lidí společně kope a každý si může odnést, co najde. Ať už hrajete sólo, nebo s partou, pořád je co objevovat. Podzemní svět má krásně vrstvenou strukturu, ve které je radost se ztratit.

Shrnutí? Keep Digging je taková digitální dovolená v dole. Vstup zdarma, žádné nebezpečí závalu, jen relaxační klid a zvuk krumpáče. Pokud potřebujete vypnout hlavu a zapnout jen autopilota na kopání, tohle je přesně ono.

[h1] Review: Keep Digging[/h1]
[h1] ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️[/h1]

If you’ve ever wanted to dig a tunnel straight to the Earth’s core but were worried the neighbors (or the police) might stop you, Keep Digging is the perfect therapy.

In just about 5 hours I not only hit rock bottom (literally 1000 meters deep), but also snagged 100% of the achievements — probably the most relaxing “completionist run” I’ve ever had. No stress, no combat, no stealth missions where one mistake ruins everything. Just me, a shovel, some dynamite… and occasionally a bunch of friends painting the walls with color spray like underground Banksy.

The game is exactly what it promises — a chill, laid-back experience. No “git gud,” no sweaty grind, just pure zen digging, selling treasures, and upgrading your gear. And yes, a level 20 shovel is way cooler than it sounds. The NPC companions keep digging even while you’re offline, so it’s almost like hiring digital interns who never complain.

Multiplayer is a blast — up to 8 people digging together, and everyone gets to bring home what they find. Whether you play solo or co-op, there’s always something to discover. The underground world is layered and fun to explore, like a giant cake made of ore and treasure.

In short? Keep Digging is like a digital vacation in a mine. Free entry, zero cave-ins, just pure relaxation and the sound of a pickaxe. If you need to turn your brain off and your inner digger on, this game’s got you covered.

I had recently created a new world in single-player Keep digging. Everything was normal at first as I began mining down and buying things. I noticed something move amongst the dense fog (I have a very slow computer so I have to play with a tiny render distance). I thought it was an npc, so I pursued it, hoping to buy someth.

It wasn’t a npc though. Looking back at me was another character with the default skin, but his eyes were empty. I saw no name pop up, and I double-checked to make sure I wasn’t in multiplayer mode. He didn’t stay long, he looked at me and quickly ran into the fog. I pursued out of curiosity, but he was gone.

I continued on with the game, not sure what to think. As I expanded the world, I saw things that seemed out of place to make; player made tunnels in the rocks, small perfect pyramids made of sand in the ocean, and groves of trees with all their leaves cut off. I would constantly think I saw the other “player” in the deep fog, but I never got a better look at him. I tried increasing my render distance to far whenever I thought I saw him, but it was to no avail.

Game Review: Keep Digging – The Game of the Century

In a world of endless game releases, few titles manage to transcend the digital space and become something truly transformative. Keep Digging is one of those rare gems that doesn’t just entertain—it changes you. This isn’t just a game; it’s an experience that will resonate in your heart long after you’ve stopped playing. I’m confident in saying that Keep Digging is not only Game of the Year, but also Game of the Century, and one that will continue to define the gaming landscape for years to come.

A Concept So Simple, Yet Profound

At its core, Keep Digging is deceptively simple: you dig, uncover resources, and progress. It sounds like something you've seen before, but what this game does with that basic premise will leave you astounded. As you dig deeper into the earth, each layer reveals new mysteries, deeper challenges, and an evolving narrative that keeps you hooked. The deeper you go, the more you learn—not just about the world you’re exploring, but about yourself.

The game subtly challenges you to dig into your own persistence and resilience. It isn’t just about finding treasure or achieving in-game goals; it’s about discovery, growth, and evolution. Every single shovel stroke feels like an effort to overcome not just the obstacles in the game, but those in your own life. This is a game about pushing through, about never giving up, and about finding beauty in the journey—even when you’re covered in dirt.

Gameplay That Elevates the Genre

The gameplay of Keep Digging is what truly sets it apart. On paper, it may sound like a basic mining and resource-gathering game, but the execution is nothing short of perfection. The controls are incredibly intuitive, and the mechanics are easy to pick up but challenging to master. With every new tool and upgrade you unlock, your gameplay experience deepens and diversifies. You’ll find yourself solving puzzles, battling underground creatures, and discovering hidden caverns, each more exciting than the last.

What I really love is the game’s pacing. It never feels rushed or grindy. There’s always a sense of progress, and each new challenge feels like a natural step forward in your journey. And with each new layer you uncover, you gain access to better equipment, more powerful abilities, and a deeper understanding of the world’s history. It’s the kind of gameplay that rewards persistence and curiosity, without ever feeling like a slog.

A World Full of Surprises

The world of Keep Digging is one of its most enchanting features. It’s not just beautiful—it’s alive. The game offers a dynamic, ever-changing environment, where every section you dig into is a new landscape full of surprises. Whether it’s discovering glowing underground rivers, stumbling upon ancient relics, or unearthing long-forgotten civilizations, the world feels rich and full of secrets. The sense of discovery in Keep Digging is unparalleled.

But let’s talk about the beauty of this world. While I wouldn’t call it "hyper-realistic" or overly focused on flashy effects, the visual design is stunning. The game’s beauty lies in its elegance—the way the light reflects off subterranean pools, the soft glow of bioluminescent plants, and the majestic scale of the underground cities you’ll uncover. It’s a quiet beauty that draws you in without needing to flaunt its visual prowess. Every new discovery feels like unwrapping a gift, and the world constantly rewards you with new, breathtaking moments. It’s the kind of beauty that stays with you long after you've put down the controller.

Soundscapes That Immersive You

The sound design is equally exceptional, adding another layer to the experience. The deep rumbles of the earth beneath your feet, the gentle click of your tools, and the subtle hum of distant machinery all come together to create an immersive environment that feels alive. Each sound evokes a sense of place and purpose, making you feel as though you are truly part of this world. The soundtrack itself is soothing yet suspenseful, perfectly complementing the pacing of the game and adding to its emotional depth.

A Life-Altering Journey

If there’s one thing that truly sets Keep Digging apart, it’s the emotional journey it takes you on. This isn’t a game where you just mindlessly click and collect. The deeper you dig, the more you uncover about the world—and about yourself. The game’s themes of perseverance, self-discovery, and the rewards of hard work are woven seamlessly into the narrative. It feels like the game is challenging you to keep moving forward, even when things seem tough.

And that’s where Keep Digging is more than just a game—it’s a life lesson. You’ll find yourself applying the game’s message to your own life, remembering that sometimes the best rewards come after digging through the toughest challenges. It’s a game that teaches you the value of persistence, and every victory, no matter how small, feels deeply satisfying.

The Game of the Century

I truly believe that Keep Digging is not just a game, but a cultural milestone. It is the Game of the Century. It will not only be remembered for its groundbreaking gameplay but for the way it changes the way we think about games. This is a title that doesn’t just entertain—it educates, inspires, and leaves an emotional mark on everyone who plays it.

If you’ve ever wondered if a video game could truly change your perspective on life, Keep Digging is that game. It’s an experience unlike any other, one that will challenge you to keep moving forward, no matter the obstacles. Whether you’re an avid gamer or a casual player, this is a game you must experience.

So, dig deep. Uncover the world. And remember: Keep Digging—because the best rewards are always waiting just beneath the surface.

近日沉醉於此遊，其樂無窮，堪稱神技，特撰此評，欲薦其妙，期共賞之。夫此遊也，非尋常之娛，乃開天闢地之奇作，引人入勝，令人忘返。初啟遊戲，余化身礦仙，手執神鏟，光華四射，猶若仙器，欲掘地心，探無盡之寶藏。每揮一鏟，礦石迸現，黃金閃耀，寶玉生輝，異石爭奇，宛如天降甘霖，令人心醉神迷。其畫面絢麗，色彩如虹，音律激昂，節奏振奮，角色玲瓏可愛，令人捧腹，斯非遊戲，乃人間之樂園也！玩法之精妙，世所罕見，層層深入地心，每層皆有新奇，或遇崩岩，需敏捷避之，猶若騰雲駕霧；或逢崑崙人，饋以油炸禽肉，則助吾挖掘，宛如忠僕。升級之法，更是巧奪天工，鏟可化激光、火箭，乃至時空之器，一擊洞穿數層；技能繁多，或震地裂石，或探寶如神，令人自覺如統地下之霸主，威震四方。然斯遊之極致，乃與奶龍一戰也！此龍乃地心之霸王，咆哮如雷，目若赤珠，爪利如劍，尾掃山崩，岩漿噴薄，氣勢懾人。戰之時，余持神鏟，騰挪閃避，伺機擊其弱點，特效華麗，煙火四射，勝之則寶藏滾滾，裝備神異，地圖新開，令人欲罷不能。此遊之樂，非止於挖礦，乃療癒心魂，節奏如禪，成就滿溢；難關砥礪智慧，奶龍之戰激發豪情壯志。更有聯盟之樂，可與友共掘，齊呼「挖！挖！挖！」，勝龍之際，友情升華，樂趣無邊。開發者神思妙想，更新頻繁，季活動、新礦區、跨界之奇，皆令人目不暇接。諸友若未嘗此遊，則人生黯淡，失卻光華！此遊免物超所值，無論士農工商，皆可沉醉其中。吾友近平，昔日沉悶，終日面露愁苦，今因斯遊，活力四射，春風滿面；吾友正恩，本臥病在床，氣虛血弱，現則夜夜掘礦，笑聲不絕。斯乃快樂之源，人生至寶！願諸友速下載之，共赴地心，掘無盡之寶，斬霸王之龍，成傳奇之名！挖！挖！挖！永不止息！

剛進遊戲時我還裝斯文，捏著小鎬頭輕輕敲岩壁，心裡默念 「要溫柔要溫柔」，結果挖了半小時只攢夠造個木盾的材料。直到某天誤觸了炸彈道具，看著整塊岩石被炸得粉碎，碎石子蹦到屏幕外的既視感，我瞬間覺醒了 「暴力挖掘之魂」。​
現在的我主打一個 「拆遷隊作風」：遇到普通土層用鎬頭划拉，碰著硬岩石直接扔炸彈，碰上水晶礦層恨不得把迫擊炮架起來轟。但這遊戲壞得很，你以為挖開的是滿箱寶石？大概率是竄出來的穴居怪咬你，或者挖通了地下河，眼睜睜看著剛挖的礦石飄走 —— 合著我這不是挖礦，是在拆地下世界的盲盒啊！
不過升級裝備後是真爽。從初始鎬頭到能發射激光的高科技傢伙，再到自動挖礦的機械臂，效率直接從 「蝸牛爬」 變 「火箭飛」。上次我用自動化機械挖了一倉庫礦石，看著冶煉爐哐哐出成品，那種 「躺平也能暴富」 的快樂，比中彩票還上頭。

【終極BOSS戰體驗】腎上腺素爆表！這根本不是戰鬥，是靈魂的試煉啊！🔥

終於打過了《黯影迴廊》最終章的黑月主宰，現在雙手還在發抖⋯⋯這絕對是我十年遊戲生涯中最癲狂的BOSS戰體驗！從機制設計到視聽衝擊，完全就是藝術級的暴力美學！

⚡️「多重形態轉換」讓人窒息！剛適應第一階段的暗影彈幕，突然撕裂空間變成三重鏡像攻擊，最後10%血量居然召喚隕石雨+地裂詛咒的雙重必殺技——我窩在電競椅上尖叫到鄰居敲牆警告！

🎮 操作精度要求簡直變態！但又不是無腦難，每個死亡瞬間都清晰感覺到自己失誤在哪（對，就是那個該死的0.5秒無敵幀按早了）。破防瞬間的處決動畫配上交響金屬BGM，全身雞皮疙瘩炸成煙花！

💥 最神的是劇情殺反轉！當你以為要結束時，BOSS突然吞噬場景光源，強制進入「全黑環境僅靠技能光效辨位」的終極模式——這種打破第四面牆的設計簡直是惡魔級的 genius！

現在閉上眼睛還是滿腦子暗紅色的危險警示框閃爍⋯⋯硬核玩家不挑戰這個BOSS等於白活！建議直接頒獎給關卡設計師，這人絕對是個瘋子！🎮💀

這款遊戲真的讓我沉迷到不行！遊戲中有一個廣闊又充滿神秘氣息的地下世界，玩家可以自由探索那龐大的地底空間。一路上不斷撿拾各式各樣的裝備與道具，從最初的簡單工具，到後來能左右戰局的強力武器，每一次收集都帶來新的驚喜。深入探索時，會遇到兇惡而詭譎的地底人，他們成群結隊潛伏在黑暗之中，隨時準備對冒險者發動攻擊。擊敗他們之後，不僅能獲得豐厚的戰利品，還有機會挖掘到傳說級的寶物，光是這個過程就充滿了成就感！

遊戲中最讓我印象深刻的，就是能夠蒐集化石並透過儀式召喚出暴龍。當暴龍轟鳴著衝向地底人的大軍時，那種壓倒性的震撼感讓人熱血沸騰，彷彿真正成為了古代霸主的指揮官。尤其在對付地底人 BOSS 的時候，暴龍簡直就是最可靠的戰力支援，不然真的會打到懷疑人生。舉個例子，我辛苦撿了二十個炸藥，結果引爆之後，居然只把最終 BOSS 的血量削掉十分之一，難度之高真的是讓人又氣又笑。

但也因為挑戰性十足，這款遊戲才格外吸引人。地底世界不僅僅是戰鬥，還融合了冒險、解謎與探索的元素。黑暗中隱藏的未知、隨機掉落的寶物，以及一次次驚險的遭遇戰，都讓每場冒險都不會重複。你永遠不知道下一秒會遇到什麼樣的奇幻挑戰。

總結來說，這款遊戲絕對是地下冒險類型中的佳作，遊玩過程中不僅能感受到緊張刺激，還能體驗到發掘寶藏的快感與挑戰極限的熱血。如果你也喜歡那種既艱難卻充滿樂趣的冒險體驗，那麼千萬不要錯過這款遊戲。我已經深深著迷了，真的超級推薦給大家！

楽しかったです。
直下掘りが最強でした。

きれいに取り除きたいのにカスが残ったり、石などの鉱石が拾わない限り残り続けるので自動採集があったらありがたいなと思いました。

剛結束這款挖泥土的遊戲，我心裡其實滿滿都是成就感與一點點不真實的震撼。一路上不斷地往地下深處鑿掘，每一次敲擊土壤、挖開岩層，都像是在挑戰自己的耐心與判斷力。過程中不只有單純的資源收集，還得思考怎麼分配工具、補給與體力，慢慢地，挖掘的動作變成了一種節奏感，甚至讓人產生一種「再往下一點就好」的上癮感。隨著地層越來越深，未知的壓力也越來越強，直到某個瞬間，巨大的震動伴隨著低沉的吼聲，代表著最終的挑戰出現了——霸王龍。

面對牠時，我完全感覺不到之前累積資源的安全感，反而被那龐大的身影震懾。牠每一次的撲擊都帶著毀滅性的力量，而我只能冷靜判斷，利用早先辛苦挖掘獲得的武器與陷阱反擊。那是一場腎上腺素全開的戰鬥：閃避、攻擊、再閃避，每一秒都像走在生死邊緣。最終，當霸王龍在最後一擊中轟然倒下，我幾乎不敢相信自己真的完成了這趟旅程。從挖泥土的單純樂趣，到與霸王龍決戰的驚心動魄，整個過程就像是一段從平凡走向史詩的冒險。

✨ This game has great ideas but the execution isn’t there.

⛏️ You only get a fantasy-style pickaxe instead of real mining gear. Where are the drills, rigs, or heavy tools? Dynamite feels weak and often destroys useful resources.

🧱 There’s no way to reinforce tunnels, so immersion takes a hit.

🌍 The map is big, but every hundred meters you just drop into empty voids with random pick-ups. It feels outdated rather than exciting.

⚖️ Amazing concept, but right now it’s more potential than fun.

それは深くなればなるほど悪化しています。
なので直下掘りするのはシステム上あっている可能性出てきました。
そして処理が間に合わず角を真下掘りすると透けて一番下まで落ちれます。なので2分で一番下まで掘らずに降りれることを報告いたします。

次に現在改善してほしいところ
1.真横に掘るときの処理を改善してほしい。
2.掘る枠を〇丸か□四角く掘れる選択肢が欲しい
　現在丸で掘っている　　□は(真横に掘る際綺麗に掘れるから)
3.ダイナマイトを投げる際に前に投げるので真下に投げさせてほしい

4.ワイヤーの横動きが早すぎて調整が難しい

✅ Easy to pick up
✅ Addictive gameplay loop
✅ Great for quick sessions or long hauls
✅ So much better with voice chat and friends
❌ Not as fun solo—but that’s kind of the point!

【最終頭目攻略】毀滅之牙—霸王龍．泰坦尼克斯 (Tyrannix Prime)

保持距離與警惕： 泰坦尼克斯的近戰攻擊範圍廣且傷害高，遠程攻擊則需要精準走位。
觀察前搖： 它的每一個主要攻擊都有明顯的前搖動作，熟悉這些動作是生存的關鍵。
元素抗性： 建議隊伍成員攜帶能增加「自然」、「火焰」或「暗影」抗性的裝備或藥劑，尤其在後期階段。
藥水與復活符文： 準備充足的治療藥水、藍藥水以及復活符文，以應對突發狀況。


階段一：原始巨獸的覺醒 (The Primal Beast's Awakening)
視覺特徵： 純粹的霸王龍形態，體表覆蓋著堅韌的鱗片，雙眼散發著不祥的紅光，體型巨大，但尚未見到明顯的能量反應。
主要技能：
巨顎撕咬 (Colossal Bite)： 對目標方向進行毀滅性的一擊，造成極高單體傷害。坦職必須穩穩接下，並使用減傷技能。
震地踐踏 (Ground Shatter Stomp)： 抬起前肢重重踏擊地面，對前方扇形範圍造成中等物理傷害並附帶擊飛效果。有明顯抬腳前搖，輸出職業需立刻向側邊閃避。
毀滅衝鋒 (Annihilation Charge)： 選定一個目標（通常是離它最遠的遠程輸出），發動直線衝鋒，路徑上的所有目標都會受到傷害並被擊退。衝鋒結束後會有短暫的僵直。
原始咆哮 (Primal Roar)： 發出震耳欲聾的咆哮，對周遭範圍內的玩家造成輕微傷害並施加「恐懼」效果（持續3秒）。可被聖騎士的「自由祝福」或戰士的「狂暴之怒」等技能解除。
弱點與攻略：
弱點： 頭部（擊中可造成短暫眩暈）和後腿（可降低其移動速度）。
攻略： 坦職將泰坦尼克斯面朝向團隊外圍，方便輸出職集中火力攻擊後腿。利用衝鋒後的僵直時間進行爆發輸出。咆哮前會有深吸一口氣的動作，及時遠離或準備解除恐懼。此階段以熟悉其基礎攻擊模式為主。
階段二：泰坦尼克斯的怒火 (Titan's Fury Unbound)
視覺特徵： 體表開始出現深紅色裂紋，並有不穩定的能量從中逸散。雙眼紅光更盛，周圍空氣隱約有扭曲感。
新技能：
熔岩吐息 (Molten Breath)： 向前方扇形區域噴射熔岩，造成持續性的火焰傷害，並在地面留下數秒的「灼熱區域」。被灼熱區域覆蓋的地面會持續造成傷害。
迴旋碎尾 (Crushing Tail Sweep)： 猛力甩動尾巴，對身後180度扇形範圍造成中等物理傷害並擊退。輸出職在攻擊後腿時需特別留意其尾巴動作。
能量脈衝 (Energy Pulse)： 泰坦尼克斯會短暫蓄力，然後從身體向外釋放一道能量環，對所有玩家造成中等自然傷害。可透過跳躍或部分技能規避。
弱點與攻略：
弱點： 暫無新弱點，但當其使用「熔岩吐息」後，頭部會有短暫的能量過載現象，此時對頭部攻擊傷害加成。
攻略： 坦職需調整Boss面向，避免熔岩吐息影響隊友走位。輸出職在攻擊後腿時，應保持移動，預防迴旋碎尾。能量脈衝前會有明顯的蓄力光效，注意語音提示和技能特效，準備應對。治療壓力開始增大。
階段三：創世吞噬者的畸變 (Abyssal Devourer's Mutation)
視覺特徵： 泰坦尼克斯的體型進一步膨脹，全身覆蓋著一層由創世能量結晶形成的堅硬「岩石鎧甲」。部分鎧甲縫隙中流淌著暗紫色能量。戰場周圍開始出現不穩定的能量裂縫。
新技能：
創世之盾 (Genesis Aegis)： 泰坦尼克斯在生命值降至特定百分比時激活，獲得一個吸收所有傷害的能量護盾。護盾存在期間，它會免疫所有傷害。
混沌裂隙 (Chaos Rifts)： 在戰場隨機位置召喚2-3個「混沌裂隙」，裂隙會持續向玩家發射追蹤能量彈。裂隙可被攻擊摧毀。
重力碾壓 (Gravity Crush)： 泰坦尼克斯會短暫漂浮，並在周圍形成一個持續擴大的引力場，將所有玩家吸向它的腳下。引力結束後，它會重重落地，對中心區域造成巨大範圍傷害。
弱點與攻略：
弱點： 「創世之盾」激活時，其鎧甲上會出現三個閃爍著亮紫色光芒的「能量核心」。必須在護盾消失前擊破所有核心。
攻略：
創世之盾： 護盾激活時，所有輸出必須立即轉火攻擊「能量核心」。這需要團隊的集中火力與良好的溝通。
混沌裂隙： 在處理核心的同時，遠程輸出和治療需要優先攻擊並摧毀「混沌裂隙」，以減輕團隊壓力。
重力碾壓： 當引力場出現時，玩家需要快速使用位移技能（閃現、衝鋒、瞬移等）或跑速技能，盡可能遠離Boss中心，以規避最後的毀滅性傷害。這是一次極高的團滅風險點。
階段四：泰坦的終焉 (The Titan's Last Stand)
視覺特徵： 鎧甲碎裂不堪，但從裂縫中噴湧出更狂暴、更不穩定的暗紫色與紅色交織的能量。泰坦尼克斯的動作變得極其瘋狂且快速，雙眼完全被能量火焰取代。整個戰場充斥著之前階段的所有環境危害。
新技能：
毀滅虹吸 (Annihilation Siphon)： 泰坦尼克斯開始引導一道巨大的能量射線，鎖定一個玩家並持續造成巨額傷害，同時從被鎖定玩家身上汲取生命。引導時間約10秒。
狂暴連擊 (Berserker Combo)： 它的近戰攻擊變得毫無章法且速度極快，經常會瞬間連續釋放「巨顎撕咬」、「震地踐踏」與「迴旋碎尾」。坦職需要交出所有減傷技能。
末日餘燼 (Doomsday Embers)： 泰坦尼克斯每隔20秒，會召喚一顆巨大的「末日餘燼」從天而降，砸向隨機位置，造成極大範圍的瞬發傷害。被擊中幾乎必死，需要注意落點預警圈。
弱點與攻略：
弱點： 其胸口的創世能量核心完全暴露，但只有在「毀滅虹吸」引導結束後的短暫僵直期間才能被有效攻擊，且此時受到傷害提高50%。
攻略：
毀滅虹吸： 被鎖定的玩家需開啟所有自身減傷，治療全力刷血。同時，所有輸出必須在泰坦尼克斯引導結束後，抓住它短暫的僵直時間，將所有爆發技能傾瀉到它完全暴露的胸口能量核心上。這是最主要的輸出窗口。
狂暴連擊： 坦職務必保持冷靜，合理分配減傷技能。治療需要預判並做好應急治療準備。
末日餘燼： 永遠保持移動，留意地面上的紅色落點預警圈，這是活下去的關鍵。
綜合挑戰： 此階段是所有技能的結合。戰場上可能充斥著熔岩區域、混沌裂隙，同時還需躲避末日餘燼，並處理泰坦尼克斯狂暴的近戰攻擊。團隊的走位、輸出優先級、治療分配以及對虹吸機制的精準把握，將決定最終的勝負。

Very similar to a Game About Digging a Hole with co-op and some other minor but interesting mechanics.  it is fun to play and could be given some minor improvements to make it even more interesting and fun.  My only complaints are the batteries.  Battery expansion is linear but the cost to recharge the battery appears to increase exponentially making it feel like you are being punished for increasing your battery.  This in turn discourages you from improving that technology limiting your power.  As you get further from an easy way to transport back to the surface, you need to reserve more energy for that.  This in turn discourages you from exploring the game which in turn pushes you to just dig straight down looking for the next fast travel point.  This does the game a disservice in my opinion.  Also the game could use some quality of life improvements like the ability to remap controls and tool tips to explain some aspects of the game.

Ladies, Gentleman and Gamers. 

So at the current stage I give this game a good 6/10, hear me out, and I truly hope the dev sees this review at the current game stage.

For the gamers - If you have played the game "a Game about digging a hole" you will love this, especially since this has multiplayer. The game itself is obviously still in development so expect some bugs, but there is a hint of comedy in the game, and a bit of grinding with your friends, but don't expect hours of fun, its a good 30 min of clicking the sh*t out of your mouse, then you move on to something else.

For the game/developer/s - I truly think the game has a lot more potential then the other "clicker" games. I feel it is way to easy, if you dig straight down, you can get enough cash quick to max upgrade the equipment and finish the game, leaving you feeling empty inside.

Things to consider adding to make it more challenging to keep you into it for longer.

*Level tiered ores, for example you need level 7 pick-axe to pick up diamonds, meaning more grinding lower tier ores to build up cash.

*Hard stone/boulders that you need to blow up to get into entrances of mine shafts, since dynamite is expensive you will need to grind out more for cash.

*Last recommendation I will say (believe me there is much more I could say) some sort of damage, fall damage, player damage (hit your friends with an axe, could die and respawn with nothing losing their ores).

But overall I truly enjoy the game, and think this can become a great game with friends, just some tweeking needed.
